title: Slot-level token trace fusion and KV hit latency attribution
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Add low-overhead, slot-level token instrumentation that fuses micro-spans into a per-token 'stampline' and attributes latency and cost impact to KV cache hits/misses and kernel execution. This ticket covers the runtime hooks, trace schema, ingestion pipeline, and dashboard surface for operators and capacity planners.

Scope and approach:
- Runtime hooks: emit lightweight spans at these boundaries for every emission slot: request-entry, prefix-lookup, kv-lookup, kv-apply (hit/miss), pre-attention-kernel, attention-kernel, post-processing, response-emit. Each span must include token_index, token_id (hashed), batch_id, request_id, model_version, sequence_pos, and kv_hit boolean. Use short keys to keep payload small.
- Trace fusion: implement a worker-side fusion step that merges the micro-spans for a token into a token-level 'stampline' event (token_duration_ms, kv_hit_ms, kernel_ms, cumulative_token_start_ms) to reduce downstream cardinality while preserving attribution.
- Sampling/overhead: default sample 1% of requests for full token-level export; provide deterministic session sampling for debug mode and a 100% opt-in flag per-customer for Dedicated. Target added CPU <3% and mean added latency <1ms on hot paths.
- Pipeline: OTLP/Jaeger -> kafka-topic token-stamplines -> consumer that writes to BigQuery (token_level_stamps table) and to an aggregation stream for Grafana metrics. Include enrichment job to join with request-level billing metadata (customer_tier, pricing_profile).
- Aggregations & dashboards: dashboards and alerts that show per-model and per-route token p50/p95/p99, KV hit contribution (ms and cost), token-index heatmaps (hot positions causing tail), and a waterfall view for a single request. Create a Grafana dashboard with explorable traces linked to Jaeger and a BigQuery-based cost allocation panel.
- Acceptance criteria:
  1) Token-level 'stampline' events appear for sampled requests in BigQuery within 2 minutes of request completion for 95% of samples.
  2) Grafana dashboard shows p50/p95/p99 per-token-index for a test workload and an alert fires when token-level p95 increases by >30% over baseline.
  3) End-to-end low-overhead validated: production can enable 1% sampling with <3% CPU overhead verified on a staged fleet.
  4) Cost allocation query produces a per-token cost delta when toggling KV cache simulation in the aggregation job.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- Use hashed token_id to avoid storing raw content. Token_index + hashed token_id allows grouping while preserving privacy.
- Fusion reduces cardinality but loses micro-timing ordering inside the token; we preserve cumulative offsets to reconstruct ordering for a single-request waterfall.
- KV hit detection: runtime will mark kv_hit true/false and include kv_latency_ms; for misses include backend-roundtrip_ms tag. Accurate attribution requires clock sync across services; add a lightweight sync/ping if drift >5ms is detected.
- Cost model inputs: GPU token compute unit (TCU) per-ms and KV backend egress cost model will be fed into the aggregation job to produce per-token cost.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge runtime hooks behind feature flag, disabled by default. Instrumented binary built and smoke tested in staging.
2) Enable 0.1% deterministic sampling for internal traffic for 2 weeks; validate fusion worker and BQ ingestion.
3) Open PR for Grafana panels and BigQuery schema; run load tests to measure overhead.
4) Expand sampling to 1% on production with alerting; enable 100% opt-in per-customer for Dedicated/VPC on request.

Monitoring and QA:
- Create a test harness that replays recorded requests and verifies stampline reconstruction.
- Queries: sample BigQuery SQL provided in Confluence to compute per-model token p95 and KV delta.
- Integrate unit tests for span creation and fusion (CI), and an integration test that simulates KV hit/miss sequences.

Deliverables:
- Runtime patch with trace hooks and feature flag (runtime PR).
- Fusion worker + Kafka consumer + BigQuery loader (pipeline PR).
- Grafana dashboard (dash PR) and alert rules.
- Confluence spec and measurement notebook with baseline numbers.
